text:
oliver: Opening a small docs PR that covers an edge-case we saw in prod: reserved-pool preemption during burst policies. Includes a short Rust SDK snippet, YAML examples, and a troubleshooting checklist. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3377

priya: Thanks! This is a useful gap. Can you add a one-liner about data-residency constraints for Private deployments (EU customers) since preemption interacts with cross-region fallback?

oliver: Good call  added a paragraph explaining that cross-region fallback is disabled for private deployments unless explicitly allowed and we show a sample field `allow_cross_region_fallback: true` in the YAML.

zhou: Can we surface who owns the orchestration decision in the flowchart? i.e., whether the platform controller or the dedicated runtime triggers eviction under burst. That changed recently.

oliver: Added: "Eviction decision: runtime observes memory/GPU pressure and requests eviction; orchestration controller validates policy and executes preemption/fallback according to scalePolicy and evictionPolicy." Kept it short.

hana: Please show a small Rust SDK snippet; we only have Python/Go examples in the handbook and some infra teams are using Rust. Also add a note about the `burst_capacity` parameter interplay with cooldowns.

oliver: Added Rust example using the new client helper `create_reserved_pool`. Snippet below:

```rust
use redwood_inference::Client;
let client = Client::from_env();
let req = client.create_reserved_pool_builder()
    .name("reserved-eu-burst")
    .gpus(8)
    .labels([("pool","reserved-eu-burst")].into())
    .scale_policy_min_replicas(2)
    .scale_policy_max_replicas(32)
    .scale_policy_burst_capacity(8)
    .eviction_policy("soft")
    .build();
client.create_reserved_pool(req).await?;
```

priya: Nice. Tiny API naming nit: our builder uses `burst_capacity` not `scale_policy_burst_capacity` in the Rust SDK. Can you align?

oliver: Fixed to `burst_capacity(8)`. Thanks.

zhou: For the YAML examples, please include an explicit mapping that shows `burst_capacity` > 0 with `cooldown_seconds` and how `grace_period_seconds` affects soft eviction. Something like: 

```yaml
reserved_pool:
  name: reserved-eu-burst
  gpus: 8
  labels:
    pool: reserved-eu-burst
  scale_policy:
    min_replicas: 2
    max_replicas: 32
    burst_capacity: 8
    cooldown_seconds: 120
  eviction_policy: soft
  grace_period_seconds: 300
  allow_cross_region_fallback: false  # for Private/EU setups
```

hana: That's perfect. Also add a short paragraph that `burst_capacity` is primarily for absorbing short, sudden traffic spikes and should be sized in GPU-counts, not user-concurrency.

tom: docs-bot flagged a stale link in the draft: `/dedicated/burst` -> should point to `/dedicated/autoscale#burst-capacity`.

docs-bot: Linkcheck: 1 broken link detected: `/dedicated/burst` -> suggested replacement `/dedicated/autoscale#burst-capacity`. Automated suggestion created on branch.

yvonne: Suggest we include a short troubleshooting checklist for when preemption occurs unexpectedly: 1) verify selector labels match reserved pool, 2) confirm burst_capacity isn't exhausted, 3) check cooldown_seconds and evaluation windows, 4) inspect model variant fallback ordering, 5) confirm cross-region fallback policy for Private deployments.

oliver: Added the checklist and a one-paragraph explanation of model variant fallback: default ordering is pinned version -> compatible quantized variant -> smaller model family. Mentioned customers can override ordering via `fallback_order` in the tenancy config.

priya: Slight wording nit: avoid the phrase "we will preempt" in docs; use "the system may preempt" to be less prescriptive. Also replace "best-effort" with "service-level target" for SLA language.

oliver: Updated language per nits. Re-ran local linkcheck and fixed one more crosslink to `/sdk/rust/old-client` -> `/sdk/rust/client`.

docs-bot: CI: linkcheck passed after patch, static build OK, staged deploy succeeded.

hana: Approved from docs side. :white_check_mark: I filed a follow-up issue to add a short benchmark note that shows how burst_capacity sizing affected p99 in our loadtest for Llama-variant workloads.

zhou: Approved from platform side. :+1: Please add a crosslink to the orchestration runbook (once the runbook PR merges).

priya: Approved. I'll coordinate a quick note to account teams about the Private/EU fallback defaults.

oliver: Merged. Release notes: added reserved-pool preemption guide, Rust SDK snippet, YAML examples, checklist, and Private/EU fallback note. Follow-ups: runbook crosslink and backport advisory for 1.x handbook. Thanks everyone! :tada:
